thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, U.S. Stocks Turn Positive As Apple, MIxed Economic Reports Brighten Market Sentiment

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, U.S. Stocks Turn Positive As Apple, MIxed Economic Reports Brighten Market Sentiment
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Friday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +1.1%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +0.4%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +1.1%
PowerShares QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +1.6%
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): -3%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were modestly higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 1.6%.
U.S. stocks turned higher at session's half, as Apple's (AAPL) strong day lifted the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average following a mixed payrolls report.
The tech giant rose 3.3% in the best increase on the Dow after media reports said Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A, BRK.B) bought 75 million shares of the technology giant in Q1. Berkshire's annual investor meeting will take place on Saturday, and the conglomerate's shares were slightly higher Friday.
The positive action in the biggest U.S. company by market capitalization helped markets recoup decreases made after the April jobs report came in below expectations, with a headline of 164,000, below the consensus for 191,000 on Econoday but higher than March. The unemployment rate dipped to 3.9%, below the 4% predicted, but average hourly earnings rose just 0.1% month-on-month against expectations for a 0.2% increase.
Markets were also digesting geopolitical headlines after China's state-run news agency Xinhua said the Asian nation and the U.S. reached agreements on some issues in trade talks this week, but both sides recognized "considerable differences still exist" and more work is needed.
Power Play: Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) rose 0.8% and other industrial funds Vanguard Industrials (VIS) and iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), were in the green.
Fluor (FLR) plunged 22% after the company said it swung to a Q1 net loss of $0.13 per diluted share, compared to net earnings $0.43 in the year-ago period and missed the CapIQ mean for a profit of $0.72. Sales were flat at $4.8 billion from last year and beat forecasts for $4.69 billion. It cut its 2018 guidance for EPS to a range of $2.10 to $2.50 from $3.10 to $3.50 and was below estimates for GAAP EPS of $3.16 and $3.19 normalized.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 1.1%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 2.7% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 2.8%.
Virtu Financial (VIRT) fell more than 4% the firm reported early Friday Q1 adjusted earnings of $0.76 per share, up from $0.16 per share in the prior year period and higher than the $0.61 per share Street estimate provided by Capital IQ. Adjusted revenue was $340.3 million, up from $82.2 million reported for the same period last year and higher than the $307.2 million Street estimate.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 1.6% while other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were lower.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 1.7% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 2%.
Universal Display's (OLED) rose more than 8% after the company reported Q1 diluted EPS fell to $0.13 in Q1, ahead of the $0.10 per share expected in a Capital IQ poll, from $0.22 a year earlier. Revenue decreased 22% to $43.6 million from a year ago, lagging the $51.85 million estimate. The company said it now expects revenue of $280 million to $310 million for fiscal 2018, down from $350 million to $380 million previously. The Street view is for revenue of $363.8 million.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.9% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.7%.
GasLog (GLOG) rose nearly 7% after the company reported Q1 adjusted loss of $0.01 per share, compared to a gain of $0.06 a year earlier, and below the Street view of a gain of $0.08. The shipper reported Q1 revenue of $138.5 million, down from $128.3 million reported a year earlier, and also below the $143.3 million Street view.
Commodities
Crude was up 1%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 2%. Natural gas was down 0.2% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.5%.
Gold was down 0.1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was up 0.2%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.3%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.3% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.7%.
Medifast Inc. (MED) soared 22.3% to a new record high after the manufacturer of wellness products reported late Thursday Q1 net profit and revenue that topped the Street consensus, and upwardly revised guidance for the full year. Q1 profit was $1.01 per diluted share, up from $0.51 a year ago. That was higher than the $0.86 per share Street estimate of two analysts as compiled by Capital IQ. Revenue for the quarter was $98.6 million, up from $70.6 million reported for the same period last year. That result surpassed the $89.2 million Street estimate. For Q2, the company expects earnings to range from $0.94 to $0.97 per diluted share on revenue of $99 million to $102 million. The Street consensus calls for revenue of $101.5 million. For 2018, the company now expects earnings of $3.55 to $3.65 per diluted share on revenue of $385 million to $395 million, as compared with previously issued guidance of $3.15 to $3.25 per diluted share on revenue of $350 million to $360 million. The Street estimates were $3.26 per diluted share and $360 million for revenue, respectively.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 1.4% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were firmer.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 1.2% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in positive territory.
Wingstop (WING) rose more than 8% after the company said late Thursday that for Q1, it recorded an adjusted net income of $7.3 million, with adjusted earnings per diluted share of $0.25 that is up 19.0% from the previous year's first quarter and exceeding consensus estimates of $0.20 per share. The company's total revenue for the first quarter also improved, up 11.9% to $37.4 million and also exceeding consensus estimates of $36.5 million.
Wingstop reiterated its guidance for the fiscal year ending Dec. 29 of fully diluted adjusted earnings per share of $0.75, which is lower than consensus estimates of $0.77. In addition, Wingstop's board of directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.07 per share, for a total of about $2.1 million, to be paid on June 18 to shareholders of record as of June 4.
